_note: Untouched or under-explored concepts, each science-grounded and shaped to the channel's aesthetic. fidelity: established | emerging | metaphor. Draw from these for new scripts.

frontier.title: Your Feelings Are Forecasts
frontier.science: Constructed-emotion theory (Barrett): the brain builds emotions by predicting the body's energy budget and interpreting interoceptive signals; emotions are constructed guesses, not fixed reactions.
frontier.hook: You don't feel anxiety. Your brain predicts a body in trouble and hands you the word 'anxiety' as the caption.
frontier.metaphor: Emotions as a weather forecast for a body that hasn't happened yet.
frontier.turn: If the feeling is a prediction, it can be re-authored — not suppressed, re-forecast.
frontier.invitation: Next strong feeling, ask: what is my body predicting right now, and is the forecast right?

frontier.title: You Don't Know Why You Did That
frontier.science: Split-brain 'interpreter' (Gazzaniga) + choice-blindness experiments (Nisbett & Wilson, Johansson): people confidently explain decisions they demonstrably didn't make that way. The mind narrates reasons after the fact.
frontier.hook: There's a press secretary in your head who never attends the meeting but always explains the decision.
frontier.metaphor: The interpreter as a spokesperson issuing confident statements about a government he's never met.
frontier.turn: Humility as a superpower: 'I don't fully know why' is the most honest — and freeing — sentence.
frontier.invitation: Catch one reason you gave today and ask: did I decide that, or did I narrate it afterward?

frontier.title: Belief Rewrites the Body
frontier.science: Placebo/nocebo effects: expectation measurably changes pain, immune markers, motor symptoms (open-label placebo still works). Belief is not just mental — it has biological teeth.
frontier.hook: A sugar pill you KNOW is a sugar pill can still dull real pain. Your beliefs have hands.
frontier.metaphor: Belief as a signature that authorizes the body to spend or withhold.
frontier.turn: This is why belief analysis matters — beliefs aren't harmless opinions, they're prescriptions.
frontier.invitation: What belief have you been taking daily without reading the label?

frontier.title: You Argue With a Model
frontier.science: Predictive processing of social cognition / theory of mind: you never access another person directly — you run a real-time model of them and mostly experience the model.
frontier.hook: The person who made you furious last night? You were arguing with your simulation of them.
frontier.metaphor: Everyone you know is a character your brain animates from limited footage.
frontier.turn: Not cynical — merciful. If they're partly your model, you have some say in who they get to be to you.
frontier.invitation: Picture someone you resent. How much of that is them — and how much is your render of them?

frontier.title: Memory Is a Time Machine Pointed Forward
frontier.science: Constructive-memory / hippocampal simulation: the same system that recalls the past builds imagined futures. Amnesiacs who lose memory also lose the ability to imagine tomorrow.
frontier.hook: The organ that remembers your childhood is the same one that dreams your next Tuesday.
frontier.metaphor: Memory as raw footage the mind re-cuts into trailers for films that haven't been shot.
frontier.turn: You're not haunted by the past — you're building tomorrow out of its parts. Choose the parts.
frontier.invitation: What piece of your past are you using as set-dressing for a future you don't actually want?

frontier.title: When the Familiar Goes Alien
frontier.science: Jamais vu & semantic satiation: stare at a common word or your own hand long enough and it de-familiarizes — the brain's prediction of 'known' fails and the raw thing appears. The inverse of deja vu.
frontier.hook: Say your own name thirty times. Watch it stop being yours.
frontier.metaphor: The mind's 'familiar' stamp wearing off, revealing the strangeness underneath the ordinary.
frontier.turn: Jamais vu is a free trip: the world made strange without leaving your chair. Wonder is a glitch you can trigger.
frontier.invitation: Look at your own hand until it becomes an object. That astonishment was always available.

frontier.title: The Continuity Editor
frontier.science: The binding problem + saccadic/change blindness: separate features (color, motion, sound, edges) are processed apart and stitched into one seamless scene. The seams are hidden from you.
frontier.hook: You experience one smooth world. It's assembled from a dozen streams that never actually met.
frontier.metaphor: A film editor doing invisible continuity cuts so you never notice the coffee cup jumped.
frontier.turn: The seamlessness is the miracle, not the default — someone in there is working hard to hide the joins.
frontier.invitation: Where in your life have you accepted a smooth story that was actually stitched from separate pieces?

frontier.title: Not Everyone Renders the Same
frontier.science: Aphantasia / hyperphantasia / inner-speech variation: some people have no mind's eye, some no inner monologue. The 'standard' inner experience is a myth — minds differ at the hardware level.
frontier.hook: Some people can't picture an apple. Some have no voice in their head. You assumed everyone was running your build.
frontier.metaphor: Different rendering engines shipping different default settings — and none of us saw the others' screens.
frontier.turn: The humility unlock: your inner world isn't the human world. Curiosity replaces the assumption.
frontier.invitation: Ask someone close: when you picture the beach, do you SEE it? Their answer may not match yours.

frontier.title: Doing Bends Time
frontier.science: Intentional/temporal binding: when you cause an action, your brain compresses the felt time between act and effect — agency literally warps your clock.
frontier.hook: The clock runs differently when you're the one pressing the button.
frontier.metaphor: Agency as a gravity well that pulls cause and effect closer in felt time.
frontier.turn: Passivity stretches time into dread; authorship compresses it into flow. Doing is a way of holding time.
frontier.invitation: Where are you waiting (time crawling) that you could be authoring (time closing)?

frontier.title: The Settings Menu Behind the Trip
frontier.science: Entropic-brain / relaxed-priors hypothesis (Carhart-Harris): psychedelics loosen the brain's high-level predictions, letting raw signal through. Explains why the world 'comes off like a skin' — the priors that normally smooth it are relaxed.
frontier.hook: The trip doesn't add anything. It turns DOWN the filter that was always subtracting.
frontier.metaphor: Not new channels — the noise-cancelling switched off, so you finally hear the room.
frontier.turn: You don't need the chemical to know the filter exists. Meditation, awe, grief loosen it too.
frontier.invitation: When has the world last 'come off like a skin' for you — and what were you doing right before?
frontier.note: DMT-lane. Keep science-honest; label speculation. Grounding beat mandatory.

frontier.title: The Edge of You Is Negotiable
frontier.science: Rubber-hand illusion & proprioceptive drift: with a few strokes of a brush, the brain will adopt a fake hand as its own. The felt boundary of the self is a live inference, not a fact.
frontier.hook: Your brain can be talked into owning a rubber hand in ninety seconds. Where do you actually end?
frontier.metaphor: The self's border as a chalk line the brain redraws whenever the evidence shifts.
frontier.turn: If the edge is negotiable, so is what you include as 'me' — the tool, the loved one, the world.
frontier.invitation: What have you been treating as 'not me' that you actually can't feel the seam of?

frontier.title: The Center That Isn't There
frontier.science: Narrative self / 'center of narrative gravity' (Dennett): the self is a useful fiction — an abstraction the brain generates to organize a story, like a center of mass with no physical object at the point.
frontier.hook: Search your head for the one who's in charge. Notice you can't find the address.
frontier.metaphor: The self as a center of gravity — real in its effects, empty at the point.
frontier.turn: Not a loss — a liberation. If no one's home, no one has to defend the house.
frontier.invitation: Who exactly is reading this sentence? Look. What do you actually find at that spot?
